name: Drought
value: El Niño drought in Africa, Asia; no crop failure
summary: El Niño drought spreads across southern Africa and Asia; no major exporter's harvest has failed
state: Reports on 4 Nov describe El Niño drought killing cattle and threatening crops across several continents, with warnings of higher food prices (Malay Mail). The Philippines expects a very strong El Niño to cut farm output and water supply, with drought declared from December (BusinessWorld, 4 Nov). FEWS NET expects East and southern Africa to be hit hardest into 2027. No harvest failure in a major exporter had been confirmed as of 6 Nov.
for_you: Food prices in import-dependent countries tend to rise months after drought damages crops. Households in East and southern Africa face the most immediate risk to food and water supplies.
rubric_hit: Severe drought in major crop regions (southern Africa, South-east Asia); no major exporter's harvest failure yet (Watch)

sources.title: Malay Mail — From flooded homes to dying cattle, El Nino wreaks havoc across continents as food prices loom
BusinessWorld — Very strong El Niño threatens farm output, water supply nationwide

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
